gre-readiness-check-quant-148.prompt: A shop adds 15% sales tax to an $80 list price. How many dollars is the tax alone?
gre-readiness-check-quant-148.explanation: Tax is 0.15 × 80 = 12 dollars. The tagged total would be 80 + 12 = 92, but the question asks only for the tax, not the amount paid at the register.

distractorExplanations.b: Treats the 15% figure as $15 of tax instead of 15 percent of 80.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses a 22.5% rate (or 80 × 0.225) rather than 15% of 80.
distractorExplanations.d: Gives the tax-inclusive total 80 + 12 instead of the tax alone.

gre-readiness-check-quant-149.explanation: Divide both sides by 3 to get x − 4 = 7, then add 4 to obtain x = 11. Expanding first also works: 3x − 12 = 21, so 3x = 33 and x = 11.

distractorExplanations.a: Stops after 21 ÷ 3 = 7 and never adds back the subtracted 4.
distractorExplanations.c: Copies the right-hand side 21 instead of solving for x.
distractorExplanations.d: Adds 4 before dividing, as if the equation were 3x − 4 = 21.

gre-readiness-check-quant-151.prompt: A bicycle wheel has radius 6 inches. What is its circumference, in inches?
gre-readiness-check-quant-151.explanation: Circumference is 2πr. With r = 6, that is 2π × 6 = 12π inches. Diameter is 12, so C = πd is the same 12π.

distractorExplanations.a: Computes πr instead of 2πr, dropping the factor of 2.
distractorExplanations.b: Gives the diameter 2r = 12 and omits the factor of π.
distractorExplanations.d: Computes area πr² = 36π instead of circumference.

gre-readiness-check-quant-152.prompt: A locker code uses 3 digits chosen from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, and digits may repeat. How many codes are possible?
gre-readiness-check-quant-152.explanation: Each of the 3 positions has 5 choices independently, so 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 codes. Repetition is allowed, so this is 5³, not a permutation of distinct digits.

distractorExplanations.a: Uses C(5, 3) = 10, which counts unordered subsets without repetition.
distractorExplanations.b: Uses 5 × 3 = 15 as if only one choice per unused digit slot.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses P(5, 3) = 60, which forbids repeated digits.

gre-readiness-check-quant-153.prompt: In a survey of 250 voters, 40% favored the levy. How many voters favored it?
gre-readiness-check-quant-153.explanation: 40% of 250 is 0.40 × 250 = 100 voters. Equivalently, (2/5) × 250 = 100. The sample size 250 is the whole, not the part.

distractorExplanations.b: Computes 0.40 × 350, using the wrong whole instead of 250.
distractorExplanations.d: Returns the survey size 250 instead of the 40% subset.

gre-readiness-check-quant-154.prompt: What is the greater solution of |2x − 6| = 10?
gre-readiness-check-quant-154.explanation: Split cases: 2x − 6 = 10 gives 2x = 16 and x = 8; 2x − 6 = −10 gives 2x = −4 and x = −2. The greater solution is 8.

distractorExplanations.a: Is the lesser root from 2x − 6 = −10, not the greater one.
distractorExplanations.c: Stops at 2x = 16 and never divides by 2.
distractorExplanations.d: Multiplies 2 × 16 instead of dividing 16 by 2.

gre-readiness-check-quant-155.prompt: A right triangle has legs 3 m and 4 m. What is its area, in square meters?
gre-readiness-check-quant-155.explanation: Area of a right triangle is (1/2) × leg × leg = (1/2) × 3 × 4 = 6. The hypotenuse is 5 by 3-4-5, but that length is not the area.

distractorExplanations.a: Returns one leg instead of (1/2) × 3 × 4.
distractorExplanations.b: Gives the hypotenuse 5 from the 3-4-5 triple, not the area.
distractorExplanations.d: Omits the 1/2 and reports the product of the legs 3 × 4.

gre-readiness-check-quant-157.prompt: A $500 deposit earns 10% interest compounded once per year. What is the account balance after 2 years?
gre-readiness-check-quant-157.explanation: After year 1 the balance is 500 × 1.10 = 550. After year 2 it is 550 × 1.10 = 605. Equivalently 500 × (1.10)² = 500 × 1.21 = 605.

distractorExplanations.a: Leaves the principal unchanged and ignores interest entirely.
distractorExplanations.b: Stops after one year of 10% interest (500 × 1.10).
distractorExplanations.c: Uses simple interest 500 × 0.10 × 2 = 100 added to 500, skipping compounding.

gre-readiness-check-quant-158.prompt: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 12?
gre-readiness-check-quant-158.explanation: There are 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely outcomes. Only (6, 6) sums to 12, so the probability is 1/36.

distractorExplanations.b: Counts two ordered pairs, but (6, 6) is a single ordered outcome.
distractorExplanations.c: Treats 12 as one of 12 sums, ignoring that sums are not equally likely.
distractorExplanations.d: Gives P(one die shows 6) = 1/6 instead of P(sum 12).

gre-readiness-check-quant-159.prompt: 8 liters of 20% saline are mixed with 4 liters of 40% saline. What fraction of the blend is salt?
gre-readiness-check-quant-159.explanation: Salt mass is 0.20 × 8 + 0.40 × 4 = 1.6 + 1.6 = 3.2 liters. Total volume is 12 liters, so 3.2/12 = 32/120 = 4/15.

distractorExplanations.a: Keeps the 20% concentration of the larger jug and ignores mixing.
distractorExplanations.c: Averages 20% and 40% as 30% without weighting by volume.
distractorExplanations.d: Keeps the 40% concentration of the smaller jug.

gre-readiness-check-quant-160.explanation: 72 = 2³ × 3², so the number of positive divisors is (3 + 1)(2 + 1) = 4 × 3 = 12. Listing also gives 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 72.

distractorExplanations.a: Counts only the prime-power pieces or 2³ instead of the divisor formula.
distractorExplanations.b: Uses 3 × 3 = 9 from the exponents without adding 1 to each.
distractorExplanations.d: Adds an extra factor, as if 72 had a third prime in its factorization.

gre-readiness-check-quant-161.prompt: For the linear rule g(t) = 2t + 7, g(9) equals which number?
gre-readiness-check-quant-161.explanation: Substitute x = 9: f(9) = 2(9) + 7 = 18 + 7 = 25. Do not multiply 2 by the whole (9 + 7).

distractorExplanations.a: Computes 9 + 7 = 16 and drops the coefficient 2.
distractorExplanations.b: Computes only 2 × 9 = 18 and forgets to add 7.
distractorExplanations.c: Evaluates 2(8) + 7 = 23, using 8 instead of 9.

gre-readiness-check-quant-162.explanation: Same base: add exponents in the product then subtract the denominator: 2^(5+3−6) = 2^2 = 4. Canceling 2^5 / 2^5 leaves 2^3 / 2^1 = 2^2 as well.

distractorExplanations.b: Leaves 2^3 = 8 after canceling only part of the 2^6.
distractorExplanations.c: Computes 2^(5+3−4) or 2^4 = 16 with an off-by-two exponent.
distractorExplanations.d: Multiplies 2^6 = 64 and ignores the quotient structure.

gre-readiness-check-quant-163.prompt: A courier drives 60 miles at 30 mph and returns the same 60 miles at 60 mph. What is the average speed for the round trip, in mph?
gre-readiness-check-quant-163.explanation: Outbound time is 60/30 = 2 hours; return is 60/60 = 1 hour. Total distance 120 miles in 3 hours, so average speed is 120/3 = 40 mph. The arithmetic mean of 30 and 60 is not the average speed.

distractorExplanations.a: Reports only the slower outbound speed of 30 mph.
distractorExplanations.c: Averages 30 and 60 as (30+60)/2 = 45, which ignores unequal times.
distractorExplanations.d: Adds the two speeds instead of using total distance over total time.

gre-readiness-check-quant-164.prompt: How many 2-person committees can be formed from 6 volunteers?
gre-readiness-check-quant-164.explanation: Order does not matter, so C(6, 2) = 6 × 5 / 2 = 15. P(6, 2) = 30 would count ordered pairs, which overcounts each committee twice.

distractorExplanations.a: Computes 6 × 2 = 12 instead of the combination C(6, 2).
distractorExplanations.b: Off-by-one from 15, as if one pairing were excluded without reason.
distractorExplanations.d: Uses P(6, 2) = 30, counting ordered seats instead of unordered pairs.

gre-readiness-check-quant-165.prompt: A storage cube has edge length 5 cm. What is its volume, in cubic centimeters?
gre-readiness-check-quant-165.explanation: Cube volume is s³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125. Surface area would be 6s² = 150, which is a different quantity.

distractorExplanations.a: Adds the three edges 5 + 5 + 5 instead of multiplying.
distractorExplanations.b: Computes s² = 25, the area of one face, not the volume.
distractorExplanations.c: Computes 3 × 25 = 75, three faces, not the solid volume.

gre-readiness-check-quant-166.prompt: When 100 is divided by 7, what is the remainder?
gre-readiness-check-quant-166.explanation: 7 × 14 = 98, and 100 − 98 = 2, so 100 = 7 × 14 + 2. The remainder must be strictly less than 7.

distractorExplanations.b: Uses 7 × 13 = 91 and 100 − 91 = 9, then reduces incorrectly to 3.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses 7 × 13 = 91 and a leftover 9, then reports 4 from a mis-subtraction.
distractorExplanations.d: Reports the divisor 7, which cannot be a remainder when dividing by 7.

gre-readiness-check-quant-167.prompt: In the coordinate plane, what is the distance from (0, 0) to (6, 8)?
gre-readiness-check-quant-167.explanation: Distance is √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10. This is the 6-8-10 scaling of a 3-4-5 triangle.

distractorExplanations.a: Averages 6 and 8, or uses √(36 + 13), not √(36 + 64).
distractorExplanations.c: Adds 6 + 8 instead of taking the Pythagorean hypotenuse.
distractorExplanations.d: Multiplies 6 × 8 = 48, which is unrelated to Euclidean distance.

gre-readiness-check-quant-168.prompt: Printer A finishes a batch in 6 hours and printer B in 12 hours. Working together at constant rates, how many hours do they need?
gre-readiness-check-quant-168.explanation: Combined rate is 1/6 + 1/12 = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 batch per hour, so the time is 4 hours. Adding the times 6 + 12 is not the together-time.

distractorExplanations.a: Takes the harmonic shortcut with the wrong product, 24/12 = 2.
distractorExplanations.b: Averages 6 and 12 as 9, then halves that to 3.
distractorExplanations.d: Averages the two times (6 + 12)/2 = 9 instead of adding rates.

gre-readiness-check-quant-169.prompt: An arithmetic sequence begins 5, 8, 11, …. What is the 10th term?
gre-readiness-check-quant-169.explanation: Common difference d = 3. The nth term is a + (n − 1)d = 5 + 9 × 3 = 5 + 27 = 32. Using n = 10 as the multiplier 10 × 3 would skip the first-term offset.

distractorExplanations.a: Gives the 4th term 5 + 3 × 3 = 14, not the 10th.
distractorExplanations.b: Uses 5 + 8 × 3 = 29, as if there were 8 steps instead of 9.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses 10 × 3 = 30 and drops the starting 5.

gre-readiness-check-quant-171.prompt: Two fair coins are flipped. What is the probability both land heads?
gre-readiness-check-quant-171.explanation: Four equally likely outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT. Only HH is two heads, so the probability is 1/4. Independence also gives (1/2) × (1/2) = 1/4.

distractorExplanations.b: Conditions on seeing at least one head (3 outcomes) and miscounts HH as 1/3.
distractorExplanations.c: Gives P(one particular coin is heads) = 1/2, not both coins.
distractorExplanations.d: Gives P(at least one head) = 3/4 instead of both heads.

gre-readiness-check-quant-172.prompt: What is the slope of the line through (2, 3) and (6, 11)?
gre-readiness-check-quant-172.explanation: Slope is (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = (11 − 3)/(6 − 2) = 8/4 = 2. Rise 8 over run 4, not rise alone.

distractorExplanations.a: Uses run over rise 4/8, or (6 − 2)/(11 − 3) inverted twice incorrectly as 1.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses the horizontal run 4 as if that run were the slope.
distractorExplanations.d: Uses the vertical rise 8 as if that rise were the slope.

gre-readiness-check-quant-173.prompt: The interior angles of a triangle sum to how many degrees?
gre-readiness-check-quant-173.explanation: Any Euclidean triangle has interior-angle sum 180°. A right angle is 90°, and a full quadrilateral sums to 360°, neither of which is the triangle sum.

distractorExplanations.a: Gives one right angle, not the sum of all three interior angles.
distractorExplanations.b: Uses 3 × 40 or an exterior-angle mix, not the interior sum.
distractorExplanations.d: Gives the sum for a quadrilateral, or a full turn, not a triangle.

gre-readiness-check-quant-174.prompt: What is the least common multiple of 12 and 18?
gre-readiness-check-quant-174.explanation: 12 = 2² × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3², so LCM = 2² × 3² = 4 × 9 = 36. The GCD is 6, which is a factor of the LCM, not the LCM itself.

distractorExplanations.a: Gives gcd(12, 18) = 6 instead of the least common multiple.
distractorExplanations.b: Takes 2 × 12 = 24, a common multiple that is not the least.
distractorExplanations.c: Adds 12 + 18 = 30, which is not a multiple of 12.

gre-readiness-check-quant-175.prompt: What is the positive square root of 49?
gre-readiness-check-quant-175.explanation: 7 × 7 = 49, so √49 = 7 (the principal, positive root). 49 itself is the radicand, not the root, and 14 would be 2 × 7.

distractorExplanations.b: Doubles 7, as if √49 were 2√49/2 without simplifying.
distractorExplanations.c: Approximates 49/2 = 24.5 and truncates, which is not a square root.
distractorExplanations.d: Returns the radicand 49 instead of its square root.

gre-readiness-check-quant-176.prompt: For the list 4, 4, 8, 12, what is the median?
gre-readiness-check-quant-176.explanation: An even count of four ordered values uses the mean of the two central numbers: (4 + 8)/2 = 6. The mode is 4 and the mean is 7, which are different statistics.

distractorExplanations.a: Reports the mode (the repeated 4), not the median.
distractorExplanations.c: Reports the mean (4+4+8+12)/4 = 7, not the median.
distractorExplanations.d: Takes the larger of the two middle values instead of averaging them.

gre-readiness-check-quant-177.prompt: A soup can is a cylinder with radius 2 cm and height 5 cm. What is its volume?
gre-readiness-check-quant-177.explanation: Cylinder volume is πr²h = π × 2² × 5 = π × 4 × 5 = 20π cubic centimeters. Lateral area 2πrh = 20π is a coincidence of numbers but a different formula; here r²h is 20.

distractorExplanations.a: Computes πr² = 4π, the base area, and omits height.
distractorExplanations.b: Computes πrh = 10π, missing one factor of the radius r.
distractorExplanations.d: Uses 2πr²h = 40π, inserting an extra factor of 2 from surface area.

gre-readiness-check-quant-178.prompt: In how many distinct orders can 5 runners line up at a starting gate?
gre-readiness-check-quant-178.explanation: Lineups are permutations of 5 distinct people: 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120. C(5, 1) or 5² do not count ordered lists of all five.

distractorExplanations.a: Counts the people instead of the permutations of those people.
distractorExplanations.b: Uses 5 × 3 = 15 rather than the factorial 5!.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses 5² = 25, as if only two positions were filled from 5.

gre-readiness-check-quant-179.explanation: 2^0 = 1, 2^1 = 2, and 2^2 = 4, so the sum is 1 + 2 + 4 = 7. A geometric-series shortcut 2^3 − 1 = 7 matches. 2^3 = 8 is the next power, not this sum.

distractorExplanations.b: Computes 2^3 = 8, the next power, instead of summing 1 + 2 + 4.
distractorExplanations.c: Adds the exponents 0 + 1 + 2 = 3 and then 4 × 3, or 2+4+6.
distractorExplanations.d: Computes 2^4 = 16, skipping the actual three-term sum.

gre-readiness-check-quant-180.explanation: 1/6 + 1/y = 1/2, so 1/y = 1/2 − 1/6 = 3/6 − 1/6 = 2/6 = 1/3. Therefore y = 3. Harmonic pairing: the number whose reciprocal with 1/6 yields 1/2 is 3.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats 1/2 − 1/6 as if it were still 1/2, so y = 2.
distractorExplanations.c: Averages 6 and 2, or solves 1/6 + 1/y = 1/3 instead.
distractorExplanations.d: Takes y = 2x = 12, as if the equation were x + y = 18 with a different relation.

gre-readiness-check-quant-181.prompt: An equilateral triangle has side length 6. What is its area?

distractorExplanations.a: Uses (√3 / 4) × 24 or half of the correct 9√3.
distractorExplanations.b: Mixes (√3 / 4) × 32, as if the side were √32.
distractorExplanations.d: Uses (√3 / 2) s² = 18√3, doubling the standard formula.

gre-readiness-check-quant-182.prompt: After a 25% increase, a price is $80. What was the original price?
gre-readiness-check-quant-182.explanation: If the original is p, then 1.25p = 80, so p = 80 / 1.25 = 64. Subtracting 25% of 80 (which is 20) gives 60 and reverses the percent on the wrong base.

distractorExplanations.a: Subtracts 25 from 80 as dollars, yielding 55.
distractorExplanations.b: Subtracts 25% of the new price: 80 × 0.75 = 60, reversing the percent on 80 instead of dividing by 1.25.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses 80 − 19 from a 24% mix, not 80 ÷ 1.25.

gre-readiness-check-quant-183.prompt: What is the greatest integer less than or equal to 3.9?
gre-readiness-check-quant-183.explanation: The floor of 3.9 is 3, the greatest integer that is not greater than 3.9. Rounding to nearest would give 4, which is a different function.

distractorExplanations.b: Rounds 3.9 to the nearest integer 4, which is ceiling-like here, not floor.
distractorExplanations.c: Jumps to 5, farther from 3.9 than 4 even for rounding.
distractorExplanations.d: Reads the tenths digit 9 as if it were the floor value.

gre-readiness-check-quant-184.prompt: Red paint and blue paint are mixed in the ratio 2:5. If the mix is 63 ounces, how many ounces are red?
gre-readiness-check-quant-184.explanation: 2 + 5 = 7 parts, and 63 / 7 = 9 ounces per part. Red is 2 parts, so 18 ounces. Blue would be 45 ounces.

distractorExplanations.a: Gives one part (63 / 7 = 9) instead of two parts of red.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses 63 / 3 = 21, as if the 2:5 ratio summed to 3 parts.
distractorExplanations.d: Gives the blue share 5 × 9 = 45 instead of red.

gre-readiness-check-quant-185.prompt: A parallelogram has base 10 cm and corresponding height 7 cm. What is its area, in square centimeters?
gre-readiness-check-quant-185.explanation: Parallelogram area is base × height = 10 × 7 = 70. Perimeter would need the sides, not this height, and 2 × 70 would double the area without reason.

distractorExplanations.a: Adds 10 + 7 = 17 instead of multiplying base by height.
distractorExplanations.b: Computes 2(10 + 7) = 34 as if it were a perimeter of those two lengths.
distractorExplanations.d: Doubles the parallelogram area as 2 × 10 × 7 = 140.

gre-readiness-check-quant-186.explanation: Power of a power multiplies exponents: (3^2)^3 = 3^6 = 729. Also 9^3 = 729. 3^(2×3) is not 3^(2+3) = 3^5 = 243.

distractorExplanations.a: Computes 3^3 = 27, using only the outer exponent on 3.
distractorExplanations.b: Computes 3^4 = 81, or 9², which is not (3²)³.
distractorExplanations.c: Adds exponents 2 + 3 to get 3^5 = 243 instead of multiplying them.

gre-readiness-check-quant-187.prompt: The data set of ages is 1, 1, 4, 8, 9. What is the mode?
gre-readiness-check-quant-187.explanation: The mode is the most frequent value. 1 appears twice and every other value appears once, so the mode is 1. The median is 4 and the mean is 4.6.

distractorExplanations.b: Gives the median of the ordered ages, not the most frequent mode.
distractorExplanations.c: Rounds the arithmetic mean 23/5 = 4.6 up to 5.
distractorExplanations.d: Picks a unique interior value 8 that is not the most frequent.

gre-readiness-check-quant-188.prompt: A $90 jacket is sold at 20% off. What is the sale price?
gre-readiness-check-quant-188.explanation: The customer pays 80% of 90, so 0.80 × 90 = 72. The $18 is the discount amount, not the price at the register.

distractorExplanations.a: Gives the discount 0.20 × 90 = 18 instead of the sale price.
distractorExplanations.c: Leaves the original $90 tag unchanged after the coupon.
distractorExplanations.d: Marks the jacket up 20% to 108 instead of discounting it.

gre-readiness-check-quant-190.prompt: Inlet C fills an empty pool in 8 hours; drain D empties a full pool in 24 hours. If both are open, how many hours fill the empty pool?
gre-readiness-check-quant-190.explanation: Net rate is 1/8 − 1/24 = 3/24 − 1/24 = 2/24 = 1/12 of the pool per hour, so filling takes 12 hours. Adding 8 + 24 or subtracting 24 − 8 mixes times, not rates.

distractorExplanations.a: Adds the rates as if both were filling: 1/8 + 1/24 = 1/6, time 6.
distractorExplanations.b: Ignores the drain and reports the inlet-only time of 8 hours.
distractorExplanations.d: Subtracts the times 24 − 8 = 16 instead of subtracting rates.

gre-readiness-check-quant-191.prompt: A gift box is a cube with edge 4 in. How many square inches of wrapping cover all six faces with no overlap?
gre-readiness-check-quant-191.explanation: Surface area of a cube is 6s² = 6 × 16 = 96. Volume s³ = 64 is cubic inches, not wrapping area.

distractorExplanations.a: Gives the area of a single face 4² = 16.
distractorExplanations.b: Uses 6 × 4 = 24, adding edges instead of using 6s².
distractorExplanations.c: Gives the volume 4³ = 64 instead of surface area.

gre-readiness-check-quant-192.prompt: If 8 painters finish a wall in 12 days, how many days would 16 painters need at the same rate?
gre-readiness-check-quant-192.explanation: Work is 8 × 12 = 96 painter-days. With 16 painters, days = 96 / 16 = 6. Doubling the crew halves the time when rate per painter is constant.

distractorExplanations.b: Keeps 8 days from the original crew size instead of the time.
distractorExplanations.c: Leaves the original 12 days even though the crew doubled.
distractorExplanations.d: Doubles the days to 24 when the crew doubled, inverting inverse proportion.

gre-readiness-check-quant-193.prompt: A card is drawn at random from a standard 52-card deck. What is the probability it is a heart?
gre-readiness-check-quant-193.explanation: A standard deck has 13 hearts among 52 cards, so 13/52 = 1/4. Probability of a specific rank (one ace of hearts class) would be 1/52 or 1/13 for a given rank across suits.

distractorExplanations.a: Gives 4/52 = 1/13, the chance of a given rank (for example, any ace), not a suit.
distractorExplanations.c: Approximates 13/39 or treats three remaining suits incorrectly as 1/3.
distractorExplanations.d: Splits red/black as 1/2, which is two suits, not hearts alone.

gre-readiness-check-quant-194.prompt: A balloon is a sphere of radius 3 cm. What is its volume?
gre-readiness-check-quant-194.explanation: Sphere volume is (4/3)πr³ = (4/3)π × 27 = 36π. Surface area 4πr² = 36π is numerically the same here, but the asked quantity is volume and the formula used is (4/3)πr³.

distractorExplanations.a: Computes πr² = 9π, a circle of radius 3, not the sphere volume.
distractorExplanations.b: Uses 4πr = 12π, mixing circumference factors into volume.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses πr³ = 27π and drops the 4/3 coefficient.
